title.narrative: Empowering Women Councilors for Digital Freedom and Rights-Based Governance in the Southern Province

description.narrative:
Women's participation at local governance in Sri Lanka is low despite a 25% quota for women representation is guaranteed. Although there are legal provisions to obtain women's participation in local governance through local governance acts and ordinances, these provisions are not being implemented in practice. Additionally, women-based organizations and councilors have very limited knowledge about the laws, local governance, their rights, as well as provincial planning and budgeting. There are no mechanisms for networking women-based organizations with the women councilors. Working in isolated approaches hinders the strength of the women to raise their voices for their rights. Women’s perception and trust in local governance institutions are also at low level. These gaps needs to be filled by strengthening women’s participation in local governance. On the other side, local governance institutions should also be strengthened through the use of different mechanisms to provide effective and efficient, participatory tools for women to secure their rights including freedom of expression. Now, the local authority women's councilors’ quota has increased, but most women councilors remain marginalized within the local government structure. The key reason for this gap is a lack of specialized knowledge on freedom of expression and internet freedom, which prevents councilors from safely and effectively raising socio-economic concerns. Without a firm grasp of their legal duties and the principles of equal rights for women and girls, these councilors struggle to challenge discriminatory practices or advocate for gender-responsive policies. Therefore, the goal of this project is to reinforce a dynamic, safe, and accountable institutional framework that upholds freedom of expression, responsible governance, and fosters women's engagement in democratic values in local government institutions in Sri Lanka. Key objectives of this project • To empower women councilors with the legal and technical knowledge required to exercise their freedom of expression and advocate for equal rights within local authorities • To establish a "Digital Freedom Network" that provides councilors with the tools for safe, independent digital communication and internet freedom. • To network with key women-led organizations with the women councilors of three districts.
Project activities will be conducted with the purpose of achieving key project outcomes and outputs. Key outcomes of the project are strengthening the Freedom of Expression among women councilors of the southern province, improving the network to respond to human rights violations and inequalities for women and girls, and increasing awareness of freedom of expression, internet freedom, and human rights.
Also, 200 + women councilors will be empowered through this project, while establishing 3 women councilor forums and 3 women-led organization forums. 500 Empowered women leaders will be networked with women councilors through workshops with the participation of the Department of Local Government, Southern Province. 30 social media contents, evidence-based human rights violations reports, and a digital participatory mechanism for women development will be released at the end of the project.
This project will empower all women councilors in the southern province, while empowering 500 women-led organizations in the province. Three women's council forums and three women-led organization forums will be established, with a 100-woman leaders 30 social media contents will be published through social media as sponsored content. Finally, a provincial-level stakeholder forum will be organized to provide the lessons learned and identified issues to relevant authorities as a public forum.
49 local authorities in the southern province, the Department of Local Government and CBOs will collaboratively work as the key stakeholders of this project.
